quests.title: Rust Foundations
quests.description: Master the fundamentals of Rust: variables, types, functions, control flow, loops, arrays, tuples, and strings.

levels.title: Variables & Types
levels.description: Learn about variable bindings, mutability, and primitive types.

levels.title: Numbers & Math
levels.description: Work with integers, floats, and arithmetic operations.

levels.title: Booleans & Comparison
levels.description: Explore boolean logic and comparison operators.

levels.title: Functions Basics
levels.description: Define and call functions with parameters and return values.

levels.title: Control Flow: If/Else
levels.description: Use if/else expressions for conditional logic.

levels.title: Loops & Iteration
levels.description: Master loop, while, and for loops.

levels.title: Arrays & Slices
levels.description: Work with fixed-size arrays and slice references.

levels.title: Tuples
levels.description: Group multiple values with tuples and destructuring.

levels.title: Strings Basics
levels.description: Understand String vs &str and basic string operations.

levels.title: Type Conversions
levels.description: Convert between types using as, From, and Into.

levels.title: Constants & Statics
levels.description: Use const and static for compile-time and global values.

levels.title: Foundations Capstone
levels.description: Combine all foundational concepts in a mini-project.

quests.title: Ownership & Borrowing
quests.description: Understand Rust's ownership system: move semantics, references, mutable borrows, slices, and lifetimes.

levels.title: Ownership Rules
levels.description: Learn the three rules of ownership in Rust.

levels.title: Move Semantics
levels.description: Understand how values move between variables.

levels.title: Copy & Clone
levels.description: Learn when types are copied vs moved.

levels.title: References & Borrowing
levels.description: Borrow values with immutable references.

levels.title: Mutable References
levels.description: Modify borrowed values with &mut.

levels.title: Slice Types
levels.description: Work with string slices and array slices.

levels.title: Lifetime Basics
levels.description: Understand lifetime annotations and their purpose.

levels.title: Lifetime Elision
levels.description: Learn when the compiler infers lifetimes automatically.

levels.title: Ownership Patterns
levels.description: Common patterns for working with ownership in real code.

levels.title: Ownership Capstone
levels.description: Apply ownership concepts in a comprehensive challenge.

quests.title: Structs & Enums
quests.description: Define custom types with structs and enums, implement methods, and master pattern matching.

levels.title: Struct Definition
levels.description: Define and instantiate structs with named fields.

levels.title: Methods & Impl
levels.description: Add behavior to structs with impl blocks.

levels.title: Tuple Structs & Unit Structs
levels.description: Use tuple structs and unit-like structs.

levels.title: Enum Basics
levels.description: Define enums with variants and associated data.

levels.title: Pattern Matching
levels.description: Use match expressions for exhaustive pattern matching.

levels.title: Option Type
levels.description: Handle nullable values with Option<T>.

levels.title: If Let & While Let
levels.description: Use concise pattern matching with if let and while let.

levels.title: Structs & Enums Capstone
levels.description: Build a complete type system for a real-world domain.

quests.title: Traits & Generics
quests.description: Master trait definitions, implementations, generics, where clauses, trait objects, and key standard library traits.

levels.title: Trait Definition
levels.description: Define traits with required and default methods.

levels.title: Implementing Traits
levels.description: Implement traits for your custom types.

levels.title: Derive Macros
levels.description: Use #[derive] for common trait implementations.

levels.title: Generics Basics
levels.description: Write generic functions and structs.

levels.title: Trait Bounds
levels.description: Constrain generics with trait bounds and where clauses.

levels.title: Trait Objects
levels.description: Use dynamic dispatch with dyn Trait.

levels.title: Display & Debug
levels.description: Implement Display and Debug for custom formatting.

levels.title: From & Into
levels.description: Implement type conversions with From and Into traits.

levels.title: Iterator Trait
levels.description: Implement the Iterator trait for custom types.

levels.title: Traits & Generics Capstone
levels.description: Design a trait-based plugin system.

quests.title: Error Handling
quests.description: Handle errors gracefully with Result, Option, the ? operator, custom errors, and error propagation patterns.

levels.title: Result Type
levels.description: Use Result<T, E> for recoverable errors.

levels.title: The ? Operator
levels.description: Propagate errors concisely with the ? operator.

levels.title: Custom Error Types
levels.description: Define your own error types with enums.

levels.title: Error Conversion
levels.description: Convert between error types with From and Into.

levels.title: thiserror Crate
levels.description: Use thiserror for ergonomic error definitions.

levels.title: anyhow Crate
levels.description: Use anyhow for application-level error handling.

levels.title: Error Propagation Patterns
levels.description: Master patterns for propagating errors across layers.

levels.title: Error Handling Capstone
levels.description: Build a robust error handling system for a CLI app.

quests.title: Collections & Iterators
quests.description: Work with Vec, HashMap, HashSet, BTreeMap, iterator adapters, closures, and functional programming patterns.

levels.title: Vectors
levels.description: Use Vec<T> for dynamic arrays.

levels.title: HashMaps
levels.description: Store key-value pairs with HashMap.

levels.title: HashSets & BTrees
levels.description: Use HashSet and BTreeMap for specialized collections.

levels.title: Closures
levels.description: Write and use closures for inline functions.

levels.title: Iterator Adapters
levels.description: Chain map, filter, fold, and other adapters.

levels.title: Functional Patterns
levels.description: Apply functional programming idioms in Rust.

levels.title: Collections Capstone
levels.description: Build a data processing pipeline with iterators.

quests.title: Async & Concurrency
quests.description: Master async/await, Tokio runtime, futures, channels, Mutex, Arc, Send/Sync, and task spawning.

levels.title: Async/Await Basics
levels.description: Write your first async functions with async/await.

levels.title: Tokio Runtime
levels.description: Use the Tokio runtime for async execution.

levels.title: Futures & Streams
levels.description: Work with futures and async streams.

levels.title: Channels
levels.description: Communicate between tasks with mpsc and oneshot channels.

levels.title: Shared State
levels.description: Share state safely with Arc and Mutex.

levels.title: Async Capstone
levels.description: Build a concurrent web scraper or chat server.

quests.title: Systems & Advanced
quests.description: Explore unsafe Rust, raw pointers, FFI, macros, procedural macros, WASM, and mini-projects.

levels.title: Unsafe Rust
levels.description: Use unsafe blocks and raw pointers responsibly.

levels.title: Macros
levels.description: Write declarative macros with macro_rules!.

levels.title: FFI & WASM
levels.description: Interface with C code and compile to WebAssembly.

levels.title: Advanced Capstone
levels.description: Build a complete systems project combining all concepts.
